function fzf_configure_bindings --description 'Installs the default key bindings for fzf.fish with user overrides passed as options.'
    # no need to install bindings if not in interactive mode or running tests
    status is-interactive || test "$CI" = true; or return

    set -f options_spec h/help 'directory=?' 'git_log=?' 'git_status=?' 'history=?' 'processes=?' 'variables=?'
    argparse --max-args=0 --ignore-unknown $options_spec -- $argv 2>/dev/null
    if test $status -ne 0
        echo "Invalid option or a positional argument was provided." >&2
        _fzf_configure_bindings_help
        return 22
    else if set --query _flag_help
        _fzf_configure_bindings_help
        return
    else
        # Initialize with default key sequences and then override or disable them based on flags
        # index 1 = directory, 2 = git_log, 3 = git_status, 4 = history, 5 = processes, 6 = variables
        set -f key_sequences \e\cf \e\cl \e\cs \cr \e\cp \cv # \c = control, \e = escape
        set --query _flag_directory && set key_sequences[1] "$_flag_directory"
        set --query _flag_git_log && set key_sequences[2] "$_flag_git_log"
        set --query _flag_git_status && set key_sequences[3] "$_flag_git_status"
        set --query _flag_history && set key_sequences[4] "$_flag_history"
        set --query _flag_processes && set key_sequences[5] "$_flag_processes"
        set --query _flag_variables && set key_sequences[6] "$_flag_variables"

        # If fzf bindings already exists, uninstall it first for a clean slate
        if functions --query _fzf_uninstall_bindings
            _fzf_uninstall_bindings
        end

        for mode in default insert
            test -n $key_sequences[1] && bind --mode $mode $key_sequences[1] _fzf_search_directory
            test -n $key_sequences[2] && bind --mode $mode $key_sequences[2] _fzf_search_git_log
            test -n $key_sequences[3] && bind --mode $mode $key_sequences[3] _fzf_search_git_status
            test -n $key_sequences[4] && bind --mode $mode $key_sequences[4] _fzf_search_history
            test -n $key_sequences[5] && bind --mode $mode $key_sequences[5] _fzf_search_processes
            test -n $key_sequences[6] && bind --mode $mode $key_sequences[6] "$_fzf_search_vars_command"
        end

        function _fzf_uninstall_bindings --inherit-variable key_sequences
            bind --erase -- $key_sequences
            bind --erase --mode insert -- $key_sequences
        end
    end
end

function fish_prompt
    set -l last_status $status

    # 1. Print Left Modules and build measurement string
    set_color white; echo -n "╭─ "
    set -l measure "╭─ "

    set -l pwd_str "󰉋  "(prompt_pwd)" "
    set_color blue; echo -n "$pwd_str"
    set measure "$measure$pwd_str"

    set -l git_branch (fish_vcs_prompt | string trim -c ' ()')
    if test -n "$git_branch"
        set -l git_str "󰊢 $git_branch "
        set_color green; echo -n "$git_str"
        set measure "$measure$git_str"
    end

    set -l duration_str ""
    if test -n "$CMD_DURATION" -a "$CMD_DURATION" -gt 2000
        set duration_str "󱎫 "(math -s1 "$CMD_DURATION / 1000")"s "
        set_color yellow; echo -n "$duration_str"
        set measure "$measure$duration_str"
    end

    set -l error_str ""
    if test $last_status -ne 0
        set error_str "󱈸 $last_status "
        set_color red; echo -n "$error_str"
        set measure "$measure$error_str"
    end

    # 2. DYNAMIC BUFFER CALCULATION
    set -l date_str (date +%F)
    
    # We measure length of plain text
    set -l occupied (string length "$measure")
    
    # DYNAMIC BUFFER: 
    # We calculate the fill but leave a 2-character "buffer zone". 
    # By subtracting the buffer from the math, the '...' will never appear.
    set -l fill_count (math $COLUMNS - $occupied - (string length "$date_str") - 2)

    set_color white
    if test $fill_count -gt 0
        # Instead of a for-loop, we use printf to be faster
        printf '─%.0s' (seq $fill_count)
    end

    # 3. Print Date and Corner
    echo -n " $date_str ╮"

    # 4. Line 2 & Root Detection
    echo ""
    set_color white; echo -n "╰──"

    # Detects sudo/root via ID
    if test (id -u) -eq 0
        set_color yellow; echo -n " # " 
    else
        if test $last_status -ne 0; set_color red; else; set_color green; end
        echo -n " ❯ "
    end
    set_color normal
end
